Subject: Implementation Questionnaire: Orbit Health - Data Bridge, Mirroring & Rollback Safeguards

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for sending the implementation questionnaire. Attached is our initial response plus a draft SOW and a high-level data-bridge design that maps the integration surface between Orbit Health and Redwood. Key points up-front:

- We propose a staged "data-bridge" approach (read-only mirroring of production traffic -> validation cluster -> controlled write enablement) to minimize risk to production.
- Typical canary cadence we recommend: 1%, 5%, 20%, 50%, 100% over 7–14 days depending on traffic patterns. Each step has stop-gates tied to error rate and latency regressions.
- Rollback path: all canary traffic is routed through a traffic mirror and split proxy so we can instantly switch back to the origin model/service within 60 seconds if critical thresholds are breached.

Requested items attached: SOW-draft-v1.docx, redwood-orbit-data-bridge-design.pdf. We'll need the network egress/inbound IP allowlist and a contact for security testing windows. Proposed next step: 30-minute call next week to confirm maintenance windows and finalize the canary gates.

Can you confirm the preferred maintenance window and whether Orbit requires data residency constraints for mirrored payloads?

Thanks,

Irene — forwarding Samantha's questions with suggested answers below (please edit before sending). Attached: network-checklist.xlsx.

Inline answers:
> 1) Mirroring architecture — PHI in logs?
- Answer: By default, we do not persist full request payloads in long-term logs from mirrored traffic. Short-term validation logs (kept for up to 72 hours) may contain redacted fields as agreed. We can provide a PII/PHI retention profile and an option to disable payload logging entirely for mirrored sessions.

> 2) Downtime windows — M–F 02:00–05:00 PT sufficient?
- Answer: Yes — that window is acceptable for the heavier canary steps. For the earliest 1% traffic split we can perform outside the window as read-only mirroring; full write-enable steps can be limited to the maintenance window.

> 3) Rollback SLA & state reconciliation
- Answer: Our recommended pattern: keep all canary writes in a scoped namespace by default, perform periodic reconciliation jobs (hourly) during the canary phase, and only switch the global routing to the Redwood path once reconciliation passes consistency checks. If an immediate rollback is invoked, the routing flips back within 60s; we mark affected records in the scoped namespace for either automatic rollback (if idempotent) or manual reconciliation. We'll list reconciliation owners and escalation contacts in the SOW.

> 4) SOC 2 evidence
- Answer: We will provide the latest SOC 2 Type II report under NDA and a redacted penetration test summary. Security team prefers to exchange through your secure portal or an SFTP link.

Marcus
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus — that is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from security and platform:

- The 72-hour short-term validation log retention is acceptable if fields are redacted by default. We will send a list of fields we consider PHI to redact.
- We want the reconciliation window and owner names explicitly called out in the SOW; Michael wants the on-call name/rotation during canary.
- Agree with the traffic gating plan but can you quantify the stop-gate thresholds? Example triggers we'd expect: error rate > 2.0% (5m rolling), 99th pct latency > 300ms (5m rolling), or escalation from Orbit engineering.

Procurement will also need a conservative rollback SLA included in SOW language — can you propose precise wording for the SLA and any credits tied to missed rollback commitments?

Samantha — thanks, all good clarifications. Summary and confirmed items (for the SOW update):

1) Data handling: Redwood will not persist mirrored payloads beyond 72 hours by default; PHI fields will be redacted in short-term validation logs. We will provide a field-redaction mapping and an option to disable payload logging entirely.

2) Maintenance window: Full write-enabled canary steps will be scheduled M–F 02:00–05:00 PT. Read-only mirroring and passive validation may run outside this window.

3) Canary cadence & stop-gates (finalized):
- Step 1 (read-only mirror): 48 hrs; monitor correctness metrics
- Step 2 (1% writes): 24 hrs; stop if 5m error rate > 2.0% or 99p latency > 300ms or any P0 incident
- Step 3 (5% writes): 48 hrs; same stop conditions
- Step 4 (20% writes): 48–72 hrs; same stop conditions
- Step 5 (50% -> 100%): staged over 48 hrs with continuous monitoring

Stop-gate actions: immediate traffic switchback (within 60s), notification to Orbit on-call, freeze additional rollouts until RCA and remediation.

4) Rollback SLA & credits: Proposed SOW language — "Redwood will restore prior routing and halt Redwood-origin writes within 60 seconds of an invoked rollback command. If Redwood fails to meet this rollback SLA in two or more distinct incidents in a rolling 90-day window, Orbit will be eligible for service credits equal to 5% of the prior month's committed Redwood Dedicated fees per missed SLA event, up to a cap of 25% per month." (Open for legal wording changes.)

5) Security evidence exchange: We will upload SOC 2 Type II and redacted PT report to your secure portal once the mutual NDA is signed.

Next steps:
- I will update the SOW with the explicit reconciliation owners, on-call rotation, and the conservative rollback SLA wording by EOD Monday (2027-06-21).
- Please confirm the PHI fields list and the secure portal link for SOC 2 upload.
- Set a 30-minute call for Tuesday 2027-06-22 09:00 PT to review the final SOW and canary gate dashboards.

Thanks — I will also attach an operations runbook excerpt and the final network checklist in the SOW update.

Regards,
